title: Expansion conjecture for the bivariate derivative polynomials
statement:
Let $d_n^{(2)}(x,y\mid q)$ be the bivariate polynomials defined from the derivatives of the bivariate denominator, and let $b_n(x\mid q)$ be the polynomials used in the displayed identities preceding the conjecture. Then

**Expansion conjecture for $d_n^{(2)}$.** There exist functions $\beta_{n,j}(q)$ depending only on $q$, with $\beta_{n,0}(q)=1$, such that

$$
d_n^{(2)}(x,y\mid q)=(-1)^n q^{-\binom{n}{2}}\sum_{j=0}^{\left\lfloor n/2\right\rfloor}\beta_{n,j}(q)b_{n-2j}(x\mid q)b_{n-2j}(y\mid q).
$$

The conjecture is motivated by explicitly computed cases $n=1,2,3,4$ and proposes a structured expansion in products of the one-variable polynomials. No proof or resolution is given in the supplied text.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00316

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).
source_name: Paweł J. Szabłowski, “Multivariate generating functions built of Chebyshev polynomials and some of its applications and generalizations”, arXiv:1706.00316 (2021).
